items.currentInterpretation: The automatic-activation arm jointly changes initial child activation, child return policy, Prime action availability, replication availability, lifecycle assignments, and child spawn assignments.
items.requiredIsolation: Allocate non-conflicting replica capacity and compare automatic initial activation, automatic return, and action-catalog removal as separately fingerprinted arms before attributing the bundle effect to one mechanism.

items.currentInterpretation: Manual fabrication currently couples a Prime decision cost, source-position requirement, output-pad placement, and rebuild policy.
items.requiredIsolation: Compare local versus remote source legality with identical fabrication decision cost, output placement, lifecycle policy, and qualified union-contract bots.

items.currentInterpretation: Mobilize exists as a local arm, while the production-shaped turret transition remains contextual and can create symmetric non-progress play.
items.requiredIsolation: Run symmetric self-play and permanent-Anchor sentinels, then isolate Mobilize availability from turret numeric strength and map placement.

items.currentInterpretation: The automatic progression bundle removes Split because both mechanics currently compete for stable child capacity.
items.requiredIsolation: Provide explicitly reserved replica capacity, then compare Split available versus unavailable under identical population progression and topology.

items.currentInterpretation: Thin fronts and outer shoulders are coherent map variants rather than single-tile causal changes.
items.requiredIsolation: Use static route/exposure reports and targeted map variants before attributing an observed effect to choke width, objective capacity, or bypass availability individually.

items.currentInterpretation: Each class arm (DECISIONS #154) jointly changes several stat axes plus one exclusive verb family: Striker couples one-bend programs with the longest range and fastest cadence; Bulwark couples durability, short omni vision, slow cadence, and class-wide reversible Anchor with a longer prime windup; Fabricator couples a fragile prime with exclusive explicit forward fabrication at earlier, faster companion economics while other classes receive companions automatically. Split is absent from every class arm and reserved for a future swarm class.
items.requiredIsolation: Before attributing a class-pair effect to one axis, compare single-axis variants (verb-only, stats-only, economics-only) under identical qualified populations, and test Split's reintroduction as its own class identity rather than a shared verb.

items.currentInterpretation: Schema-3 movement is facing-decoupled (any cardinal step without turning) by architectural declaration, with no DECISIONS entry and no measurement — while the duel-game record convicted exactly this mechanic: DECISIONS #49 held strafe for oscillation-dodging and +80% game length, and the 0.5 record calls it the dodge-everything regression. The wave-1 factorial's dominant standoff-kiting doctrine and 500-tick draws are consistent with that verdict. Every exact-analysis and qualification layer currently assumes free lateral movement.
items.requiredIsolation: Pre-register facing-coupled movement arms (first candidate: move sets facing to the movement direction, rotate remains for free aim) as typed engine additions, run the same-population A/B against the current model, and recompute the exact duel analysis and evade probes under the winning model before any promotion.

items.currentInterpretation: The volley arm bundles four factors in one flag: a reversible immobile stance route, a three-lane simultaneous fan, a slower stance cadence, and — since adoption — the threshold-triggered automatic return that makes one entry buy exactly one fan. A measured effect cannot be attributed to width, to the commitment window, to the tempo trade, or to the enforced single cast on its own.
items.requiredIsolation: Compare the stance with an ordinary single-bolt gun at the same cadence against the same stance with the fan, then vary cooldown alone, then run the fan WITHOUT the automatic return (etiquette-driven exits) as a separately fingerprinted arm — the prototype's own behaviour — so the cast rule's contribution is measured rather than assumed.

items.currentInterpretation: The shell arm bundles the facing-arc projectile guard, the deflected return bolt, the form's price (immobile, gunless, arc locked on entry, objective weight retained), the reversible two-windup cycle, and — since adoption — the three-deflection shield break. A blunted striker edge could come from the guard, from the ownership flip, from the retained scoring presence, from the cycle's readability, or from the budget that ends it.
items.requiredIsolation: Run the same stance without the guard, and the guard on a stance that forfeits objective weight, as separate arms; vary entry/exit windups independently; and vary the shield-break threshold (including an unbounded shell) as its own level, since the budget is what converts the stance from an off-switch into a tempo tax. Flank-approach share must be reported per arm since the guard's value is entirely positional.

items.currentInterpretation: The five-slot arm bundles slot COUNT (three to five) with an unlock schedule (300/420, continuing the class cadence) and a slower rebuild clock (30 rather than 15) for the extra slots. It also changes topology, so it is not fingerprint-comparable to any three-slot arm on topology alone.
items.requiredIsolation: Vary the extra slots' unlock ticks and rebuild delay separately at a fixed count of five, and compare against a four-slot arm, to separate arithmetic out-bodying from schedule. The treadmill metrics that convicted SURGE are the pass/fail gate for the rebuild factor.

items.currentInterpretation: One threshold-triggered automatic return serves both stances (volley fires-count 1, shell deflections-count 3), which is deliberate mechanism economy but makes the two skills share a factor. An effect attributed to 'the cast rule' and one attributed to 'the shield break' are the same primitive at two thresholds on two counters, so a result on one arm is weak evidence about the other.
items.requiredIsolation: Report the counter and threshold per arm, and vary threshold as its own registered level on at least one stance before generalising any finding about automatic returns. The prototype arms (fan/parry, no automatic return) are the control level and remain reachable only by re-authoring, so schedule that comparison rather than assuming it.

items.currentInterpretation: The universal-bend arm changes two things at once for a class that gains the grammar: it acquires curved shots AT ALL, and its mobile gun moves from the parameterless shoot-straight action to the payload-bearing shoot action. A change in that class's win rate could be the trajectory option or the action-catalog change a contract-driven bot has to notice.
items.requiredIsolation: Depth is already separable — the striker keeps 1-4 and the gaining classes get 1-2 — so run a third level that grants the shoot action with an envelope of exactly one legal bend distance, isolating grammar from catalog. Report the share of shots that actually carry a non-zero bend count per class, since the skill-shot forensics measured most bends as too short to read.

items.currentInterpretation: The MUSTER arm's site placement is one bundled map factor: two 2-tile sites on the centre column, the alcove-shoulder widening at (10,3)/(12,3) and their mirrors that gives each site tile at least two approach headings, and the errand distance that widening also shortens (roughly six steps from the centre objective instead of eleven around the outer lane). It also mints a whole new map generation (frontline-labs-02-muster), so it is not fingerprint-comparable to any frontline-labs-01 arm on topology alone.
items.requiredIsolation: Vary site distance, site tile count, and the shoulder widening as separately fingerprinted map variants at a fixed latch duration and rally scope, and report errand round-trip cost and flank-approach share per variant, before attributing any measured muster effect to 'the flag' rather than to how far away it is or how flankable it is.

items.currentInterpretation: The 12-tick latch bundles three levers in one number: the sole-presence threshold itself, the reset-on-interruption rule (any empty or contested tick puts a running claim back to zero, which is what makes one body walking in a real denial), and latched-until-recaptured ownership (an owner keeps the site while it is empty AND while the enemy stands on it). A snowball read cannot be attributed to the threshold without separating the reset rule and the latch from it.
items.requiredIsolation: Vary the threshold alone at a fixed site and scope; then run a hold-while-present ownership level and a decays-to-neutral level as separately fingerprinted arms; then run a stall-instead-of-reset claim clock. Report time-to-first-capture, ownership turnover count, and the share of match ticks each team held the flag, since a flag that never changes hands and a flag nobody bothers with produce the same win rate for opposite reasons.

items.currentInterpretation: MUSTER moves only the Prime's automatic return, and it simultaneously REMOVES the unconditional forward-rally placement the keel hands both teams. So the arm is a scope choice and a baseline change at once: against a keel control it subtracts a free rally and re-sells it, while against a control-pendulum baseline it adds a rally that did not exist. Prime-only scoping is also the deliberate L5 mitigation (a fabricator's fourth body does not use the 18-tick clock), so scope and class-tilt are confounded by construction.
items.requiredIsolation: Run the scope as its own registered level (Prime-only versus every automatic arrival, including companion activations) at a fixed site and latch; and run muster against BOTH baselines - keel-with-unconditional-rally and pendulum-control-without-rally - since the arm's sign flips between them. Read the class edges, not only the pacing gates: a side objective that improves cap share while pushing bulwark-vs-striker further above the band is a failure with good-looking numbers.

items.currentInterpretation: MUSTER is the first effect of the shared FrontlineSecondaryControlDefinition capability, whose other registered effects (RELAY, BATTERY, KILN, ...) differ only in what owning the site does. Any improvement measured on MUSTER is therefore ambiguous between the EFFECT and the family's shared parts: a contested site existing at all, the map opening that puts it there, and one body's attendance being priced.
items.requiredIsolation: Carry RELAY - the same site, the same latch, the same map, paying a trickle of TerritorialProgress instead - as the designated control arm, and measure it rather than asserting its failure mode. RELAY is the family's L2 hypothesis made falsifiable: because Frontline ranks timeouts on territorial progress alone, a team that takes the relay and refuses to fight should win by clock. If it does, the family's other effects are the reason anything improved; if it does not, the L2 argument that shaped every effect in the memo is wrong and the slate needs rereading.

items.currentInterpretation: The capture channel ships threshold 8 with gain 1 as ONE paired claim about how much a risky tick must pay: threshold and gain are not separable claims about the same thing, and 8 was derived from the 18-tick Prime automatic return rather than measured. A channel result therefore cannot distinguish 'stillness-gated gain works' from 'captures at this speed work'.
items.requiredIsolation: Vary threshold alone at fixed gain (6, 8, 10, 12, and the unchanged 15) inside the channel arm, and report time-from-first-kill-to-capture against the 18-tick respawn window, screened-versus-unscreened completion share, and captures per match. Territorial progress scales with threshold, so every cross-threshold comparison applies the scale factor before it compares anything.

items.currentInterpretation: Revert-equals-damage bundles three things in one rule: that an interrupt exists at all, its magnitude, and its per-weapon scaling (a salvo fan bolt reverts 2, a turret bolt 1). It also bundles the scope that makes screening work — damage OFF the objective reverts nothing — with the revert itself. Full reset and pause-for-M were rejected on arithmetic (one poker with a clear heading denies the objective for the whole match), not measured.
items.requiredIsolation: Run a flat revert-1-per-hit level and a pause-1-tick level as separately fingerprinted arms at a fixed threshold, plus an interrupt-free channel level so the interrupt's existence is falsifiable. Report progress reverted per match and per weapon, progress-reverted against progress-gained (failure mode 8, poke-lock, is that ratio exceeding 1), and screen-adjacency share. Whole-run versus per-body granularity is the separate `channel-stack-interrupt` level.

items.currentInterpretation: Capping the stationary gain multiplier at 2 simultaneously honours 'more bots capturing at once capture faster' and denies a body-count class a stacking payoff for its third, fourth, and fifth channeler. The cap is also what makes whole-run revert non-degenerate, so the cap and the interrupt granularity are entangled: under the cap, per-body reverting makes a three-body stack immune to interruption outright.
items.requiredIsolation: Run an uncapped level and a cap-1 level at a fixed threshold and interrupt. Report captures per match, mean channelers per capture, mean screens per capture, and the bulwark-versus-fabricator edge — the leg the cap exists to protect.

items.currentInterpretation: One integer — the opposing erosion multiplier, shipped at 4 — sets the whole recapture price. At threshold 8 a full flip costs 2 erode ticks plus 8 build ticks against a fresh capture's 8, i.e. 1.25x, sliding toward 1.0x as the standing claim shrinks. The owner's acceptance criterion is that band: recaptures must cost 1.0-1.25x a fresh capture. The derivation is arithmetic, not measured, and it assumes the documented 'erosion reaches neutral without starting a claim on the same tick' invariant stays in place.
items.requiredIsolation: Run N in {1, 2, 4, 8} plus the overshoot-carry variant (which overturns that invariant and reaches 1.13x). Report flip cost as a multiple of fresh capture cost MEASURED FROM REPLAY rather than derived, lead changes per match, and time at each position index. Acceptance is the 1.0-1.25x band.

items.currentInterpretation: The 40-tick ratchet hold was calibrated against the measured advance-reversal latency (respawn 18 plus transit 12), not against the capture clock, and neither respawn nor transit moves under the channel. But the channel makes captures follow kills, so holds now fire in bursts and more completed enemy captures land inside a live hold and are spent. Forty may be absorbing more offence than it was priced to absorb. It was deliberately NOT re-tuned.
items.requiredIsolation: Do not pull this lever pre-emptively. The diagnostic is SPENT CAPTURES PER MATCH (captures denied by a live hold): if it exceeds roughly one per hold on average, try 25-30 as its own fingerprinted level; if it stays near the keel baseline, 40 is still correct and the swingier pendulum arrived without the hold moving.

items.currentInterpretation: The registered ALTERNATIVE mechanism for the same 2-versus-3 problem the channel was adopted to solve: one derived tile per objective region granting +1 objective weight to whoever stands on it (the region tile with the most adjacent walls, ties broken by smallest Chebyshev distance to the map centre, then lowest y, then lowest x). It fixes the arithmetic — two defenders holding the keystone stall three attackers — without changing what the front IS, produces a one-tile scramble rather than a formation, and hands a guarding form a weight-2 fortress tile. It is declared in the rules rather than the map, so the map fingerprint does not move. NOT BUILT.
items.requiredIsolation: It is the fallback if the channel's wave read shows stalls (failure mode 8, poke-lock, or failure mode 9, rush over-nerfed). Run it alone against the channel arm and against the unmodified front, at a fixed threshold, and report captures per match, stall share, and flank-approach share. Building it is one field on the capture definition and one branch in the objective-weight sum, with zero new observation facts.

items.currentInterpretation: The channel gates gain on positional stillness (moved-this-tick contributes nothing); reduced-gain-while-moving variants were analyzed (memo P2.4) but only the binary rule ships.
items.requiredIsolation: A factorial leg comparing binary stillness vs fractional gain-while-moving on the siege arm, same cohort.

items.currentInterpretation: A shelled bulwark channeling blanks frontal pokes but breaks on its third deflection ~2 ticks short of an 8-tick channel — depth-not-dominance is an analytical claim, unmeasured.
items.requiredIsolation: Siege cells with shell-carrying bulwarks vs two-heading pokers; measure completed channels by shelled vs unshelled channelers.

items.currentInterpretation: The fan reverts up to 6 against a threshold-8 channel — the salvo doubles as the premier interrupt; bundled with the channel adoption.
items.requiredIsolation: Siege x volley cast/salvo 2x2 (the byte-pinned cast alternative separates chassis from fan at zero engineering cost).

items.currentInterpretation: The turret (cooldown 1) denies a solo channel outright (-1/tick vs +1); predicted to give the turret its first real job, unmeasured against a 0.13% usage baseline.
items.requiredIsolation: Turret-usage and channel-denial counts in the wave-8 siege read vs the swell baseline.

items.currentInterpretation: Whole-run revert under the stack cap was chosen over per-body revert (degenerate: a hit on one of three stacked drops weight 3->2, still capped at 2, doing nothing).
items.requiredIsolation: A per-body-revert enum level built and run as a factorial leg if stacking dominates the wave-8 read.

items.currentInterpretation: The channel arm alone is an implicit striker buff (range 8 + cadence 2 + off-heading bends + fan interrupts). Pre-registered siege predictions: bvs +0.05..+0.20, fvs -0.20..-0.35, bvf +0.10..+0.25; tripwire: any pair below +0.15.
items.requiredIsolation: The wave-8 2x2 (swell/siege/forge/bastion) attribution cells; compare siege-only deltas against these bands before reading bastion.
